Jessica Briers.b:
At UNH

Personal
Born in Richmond, Virginia, and raised in St. Louis, Missouri. Daughter of Matt and Karen Briers.
Briers plans to pursue a career in the financial industry following graduation.
Outside the pool, she enjoys biking, traveling and shopping. Her favorite book is Into Thin Air, her favorite movie is Jurassic Park, and her favorite television show is How I Met Your Mother.

Grace Blume.b:
At UNH
Blume has established herself as one of the top divers in America East during her collegiate career.
As a junior, she captured the America East championship in the 1-meter diving event and set UNH school records in both the 1-meter and 3-meter disciplines. She followed that performance with another conference title in the 1-meter event as a sophomore while also placing second in the 3-meter competition at the America East Championships.
During her first season with the Wildcats, Blume earned third place in the 3-meter event and fourth place in the 1-meter event at the America East Championships.
Academically, she has earned recognition on the America East Commissioner's Honor Roll and was named to the College Sports Communicators (CSC) Academic All-District Team in 2026.
Before UNH
Blume competed at Dedham High School and trained with South Shore Diving Club under coach Craig Dolloff.
A standout diver at the high school level, she placed third at the Massachusetts state championships before continuing her career at UNH.
Personal
Born in Boston, Massachusetts, and raised in Dedham, Massachusetts. Daughter of Rob and Debbie Blume. Has an older brother, Sam.
Blume is majoring in human development and family studies and plans to attend nursing school following graduation.
Athletics run in the family. Her father competed in track and field at UMass Lowell.
Outside of diving, she enjoys running and participating in Zumba classes. Her favorite movie is Sing, and her favorite television show is Gilmore Girls.
Why UNH?
"The community. I have built great relationships with my teammates, coaches, peers and classmates during my time at UNH."
Fun Fact
Blume's favorite way to stay active outside of diving is through Zumba and running.

Madeline Chen.b:
Before UNH
Chen competed at Leonardtown High School, where she established herself as one of Southern Maryland's top swimmers. A team captain for the Raiders, she earned multiple regional championships and helped lead Leonardtown to conference success throughout her high school career.
As a senior, Chen won the regional championship in the 50 freestyle and earned second- and fourth-place finishes at the MPSSAA 4A/3A State Championships. She helped lead Leonardtown to the SMAC team championship, earned the Outstanding Player Award and served as a team captain.
During her junior season, Chen captured regional titles in both the 50 freestyle and 100 freestyle while earning another Outstanding Player Award. Earlier in her career, she won a regional championship in the 50 freestyle, qualified for USA Swimming Futures and was inducted into the National Honor Society.
Chen competed for Great Mills Aquatic Club under coach Elizabeth DeLoggio.
Academic Honors
Chen graduated in the top 5 percent of her high school class and earned the Seal of Biliteracy in Chinese.
Personal
Born in San Diego, California. Daughter of Tommy and Sarah Chen. Has a younger brother, Alex.
Chen is pursuing a degree in biomedical science with a concentration in medical microbiology and aspires to become an epidemiologist with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Outside the pool, she enjoys volleyball and baking. She has traveled to three of the world's seven continents and was a member of her school's chamber choir.
Her favorite athlete is Olympic champion Katie Ledecky, and she says her mother has been her greatest role model and source of inspiration.
Why UNH?
"I love the location of the university, which is close to but not directly in a city, as well as the wide variety of academic opportunities available."
Fun Fact
Chen's younger brother was invited to audition to represent Team USA in tap dancing at an event in Prague.

Lilah Doherty.b:
Before UNH
Doherty joins the Wildcats after a standout career at Longmeadow High School, where she established herself as one of the top swimmers in Massachusetts.
A multiple-time state champion, Doherty excelled in both freestyle and butterfly events throughout her high school career. As a senior, she won Division I state titles in the 50 freestyle, 100 butterfly and 200 freestyle relay while also capturing Western Massachusetts championships in all three events. She earned All-Western Massachusetts First Team honors, was selected to the Super 7 team, and set Longmeadow High School and Western Massachusetts records in the 100 butterfly.
During her junior season, Doherty became the only swimmer at the Division II State Championships to win four events, capturing titles in the 100 butterfly, 200 freestyle, 200 freestyle relay and 400 freestyle relay. She also won Western Massachusetts titles in all four events and helped Longmeadow place second at Western Massachusetts and third at the Division II State Championships.
As a sophomore, she helped Longmeadow capture Western Massachusetts and league championships while leading the program to its highest-ever finish at the Division II State Championships with a runner-up team finish. She won state championships in the 100 butterfly, 200 freestyle, 200 medley relay and 400 freestyle relay while breaking the school and regional records in the 100 butterfly for the first time.
Doherty competed for Sunrise Swim Club and Bluefish Swim Club under coaches Peter Davis, Amy Parent and Nick Rice.
Academic Honors
Doherty combined athletic success with outstanding academic achievement. She earned First Honors during all four years of high school, maintained a weighted GPA above 4.0 throughout her academic career and was inducted into the National Honor Society.
She also served on the executive board of her school's Writing Center.
Personal
Daughter of John and Carrie Doherty. Has three sisters, Seraphina, Lux and Emily, and a brother, Jack.
Doherty plans to major in chemistry and hopes to become a physician assistant. She also aims to continue improving throughout her collegiate swimming career while maintaining a strong academic record.
Athletics run in the family. Her brother, Jack, competed at the U.S. Olympic Trials and swam collegiately at William & Mary, while her father played rugby at Southern Connecticut State University.
Outside the pool, Doherty enjoys cooking, gardening, tending houseplants, reading, skiing and doing her own nails.
Why UNH?
"The location, being close to the beach, Portsmouth, Maine and the mountains."
Fun Fact
Doherty's family vacations in Costa Rica each year. One of her favorite family memories involves her mother successfully staging a photo of a monkey "playing" Jenga with pistachios outside their vacation home.

Lydia Hart.b:
At UNH
Hart earned America East Most Outstanding Swimmer and America East Rookie of the Year honors in 2024-25 after arriving at UNH following an accomplished international career that included representing Canada at the 2022 Junior Pan Pacific Championships and competing at three Canadian Olympic Trials.
Before UNH
Hart is a native of Cornwall, Ontario, Canada, and graduated from Cornwall Collegiate and Vocational School in 2024.
An accomplished international swimmer, Hart represented Canada at the 2022 Junior Pan Pacific Championships and competed at the 2022, 2023 and 2024 Canadian Olympic Trials.
Personal
Born in Cornwall, Ontario, Canada. Daughter of Chad Kilger and Jana Hart. Has a sister, Kennady, and a brother, Kaden.
Hart is majoring in sociology and justice studies with a minor in forensics. She hopes to attend graduate school and pursue a career as a forensic anthropologist.
Athletically, her goal is to earn a podium finish in the mile at the NCAA Championships. Beyond academics and athletics, she hopes to one day have a large family and live on a farm.
Athletics are a family tradition. Her father, Chad Kilger, played in the NHL.
Outside the pool, Hart enjoys reading, thrifting and camping. Her favorite book is The Silent Patient, her favorite movie is 10 Things I Hate About You, and her favorite television show is Grey's Anatomy.
Why UNH?
"I love the people at UNH because it feels like a family away from home. The campus is beautiful, and I enjoy being close to both the beach and the mountains."
Fun Fact
Hart says she can fall asleep almost anywhere.

Stephanie Gualtieri.b:
Before UNH
Gualtieri arrives at UNH following a standout diving career at John Bapst Memorial High School in Bangor, Maine.
As a senior, she was named Maine State Female Athlete of the Year after winning the Class B state diving championship. She earned first-team Penobscot Valley Conference (PVC) honors, captured the Kennebec Valley Athletic Conference (KVAC) championship and was named PVC Female Athlete of the Year. Gualtieri also earned Academic All-America honors and all-state recognition. She set school records in both six-dive and 11-dive competitions and finished 12th on Maine's all-time list for 11-dive scoring.
During her junior season, she repeated as the Class B state champion, earned second-team All-PVC honors, was named PVC Female Athlete of the Year and received the U.S. Marine Corps Distinguished Athlete Award. She also established school records in both the six-dive and 11-dive formats and earned all-state recognition.
Academically, Gualtieri received the Chinese Class Award and English II Class Award during the 2023-24 academic year and was recognized as an Academic All-American in 2025-26.
Personal
Born in New York. Daughter of Paul and Kelly Gualtieri. Has an older brother, Paul.
Gualtieri plans to study homeland security and Chinese at UNH and hopes to pursue a career in law enforcement.
Before arriving at UNH, she served as a Senate Page for U.S. Sen. Susan Collins, spending a month working in the U.S. Capitol and observing the legislative process firsthand. During her time in Washington, D.C., she had the opportunity to see all 100 U.S. senators working in the Senate chamber.
Athletics also run in her family. Her mother, Kelly Gualtieri, and grandfather, Thomas Flahive, both participated in intercollegiate athletics.
Outside of diving, she enjoys hiking, running, reading, kayaking, swimming, working out and watching movies.
Why UNH?
"I love the location."
Fun Fact
As a Senate Page in Washington, D.C., Gualtieri spent time on the Senate floor and witnessed all 100 U.S. senators conducting business in the chamber.

Clara Ginnis.b:
Before UNH
Ginnis joins the Wildcats following a successful international swimming career representing Jersey in regional and national competition. She attended Repton School in Derbyshire, England, after previously attending Jersey College for Girls.
Competing for Repton Swimming and Tigers Swimming Club Jersey, Ginnis trained under coaches Jamie Main, Ash Morris, Craig Prime, Marcus Birmingham and Nathan Jegou.
During her senior season, Ginnis qualified for the British Summer Championships and advanced to the B final at the 2026 British Swimming Championships.
In 2025, she delivered one of the top performances of her career at the International Island Games in Orkney, winning gold medals in the 400-, 800- and 1,500-meter freestyle events and adding a bronze medal in the 400 individual medley. She also established two Jersey senior records during the competition. Ginnis additionally qualified for both the British Swimming Championships and British Summer Championships in 2025.
Earlier in her career, she earned a silver medal and three bronze medals at the 2023 International Island Games in Guernsey while qualifying for the British Summer Championships in both 2023 and 2024.
Personal
Born in Jersey, Channel Islands, United Kingdom. Daughter of Neil and Rebecca Ginnis. Has two older sisters, Poppy and Gracie.
Ginnis plans to study microbiology and biomedical science at UNH. Her athletic goals include qualifying for the NCAA Championships and representing Jersey at the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
One of her most unique swimming experiences came through training with Olympic champion and world-record holder Adam Peaty while competing for Repton Swimming.
Outside the pool, Ginnis enjoys running with her dog, Ludo, cooking for her family and playing the violin. Her favorite book is One Day by David Nicholls, her favorite movie is The Parent Trap, and her favorite television show is Friends.
Why UNH?
"The sense of community and family. I am excited to be part of a swim and dive team because most of my experience has come through individual competition. I am looking forward to being part of a team environment."
Fun Fact
Ginnis once participated in a relay swim around the island of Jersey, covering portions of a 48-mile course without wearing a wetsuit.

Lily Jackson-Oates.b:
Before UNH
Jackson-Oates came to UNH from England, where she competed for Nova Centurion under coach Joseph Stanford.
One of the top age-group breaststrokers in England, Jackson-Oates represented Team England in March 2024 at an international competition in Sweden. She also reached the finals of the British National Championships in the 400 individual medley and earned a Diploma in Sporting Excellence (DiSE).
As a junior, she finished second in the 200 breaststroke at the English National Championships.
Academically, she ranked third in her class based on GCSE examination results.
Personal
Born in Nottingham, England, and raised in Redhill, England. Daughter of William Oates and Zoe Jackson-Oates. Has one sister, Megan.

Her family has a distinguished history of public service. Her grandmother was awarded an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) and was recognized at Buckingham Palace.
Outside the pool, Jackson-Oates enjoys baking. Her favorite movie is Pride and Prejudice, her favorite television show is The Big Bang Theory, and she lists Formula One driver Oscar Piastri as her favorite athlete.
Fun Fact
During the summer of 2022, Jackson-Oates traveled to Borneo for a four-week volunteer experience and earned her scuba diving certification.

Kellie Kasabian.b:
At UNH
Kasabian has earned America East Honor Roll recognition and has been named to the Dean's List every semester. She is majoring in health science and plans to pursue a career as a physician assistant specializing in sports medicine.
Before UNH
Kasabian competed at Dover High School and with SOLO Aquatics (now Commonwealth Swimming) under coach Paul Mueller. A multi-sport athlete, she also played ice hockey and baseball while growing up.
As a senior captain at Dover High School, Kasabian earned the team's MVP award and finished second in the 50-yard freestyle at the NHIAA State Championships. She also scored in the 100-yard breaststroke and helped Dover place second in the state as a member of the runner-up 200 medley relay and 200 freestyle relay teams. She was a New England Senior Championships qualifier and received the NH Scholar-Athlete Award.
During her junior season, Kasabian placed third in both the 100-yard freestyle and 100-yard breaststroke at the state championships, earned team MVP honors, competed for the Seacoast Spartans Elite hockey program and received the NH Scholar-Athlete Award.
Academically, she graduated from Dover High School ranked 15th in a class of 352 students and was a member of the National Honor Society.
Personal
Born in Dover, N.H. Daughter of Vincent Kasabian and Lynda McAdam.
Kasabian has deep ties to the University of New Hampshire. More than 15 members of her family are UNH alumni, and she grew up attending Wildcat hockey and football games. Her first swim team practiced at Swasey Pool when she was 7 years old.
Outside the pool, she enjoys watching sporting events, traveling with family and baking.
Why UNH?
"UNH gives me the opportunity to follow my dream of becoming a physician assistant while also allowing me to compete as a collegiate swimmer and represent my home state."
Fun Fact
Kasabian's connection to UNH began long before she became a student-athlete. Her father regularly brought her to Wildcat athletic events growing up, and her first swim team practiced at Swasey Pool.

Individually, she recorded a top-eight finish in the 400 individual medley and top-16 finishes in the 100 freestyle and 200 individual medley while earning Dean's List honors.

Jeffers competed at Bedford High School and for the YMCA of Greater Nashua Storm club team. Coached throughout her youth career by her mother, Erin Jeffers, she developed into one of New Hampshire's top swimmers.
As a senior at Bedford High School, Jeffers won New Hampshire state titles in the 200 individual medley and 100 butterfly while helping the Bulldogs capture their fourth consecutive team state championship. She was also a finalist at YMCA Nationals, graduated with a 3.8 GPA while taking International Baccalaureate courses and was a member of the National Honor Society.

Born in Scottsdale, Ariz. Daughter of Eric and Erin Jeffers. Has a younger sister, Paige, who is also a swimmer.

Sydney Leblic.b:
Before UNH
Leblic transferred to UNH after competing at Virginia Tech from 2023-25. A native of Madrid, Spain, she attended IES Ortega y Gasset and competed for CTD Madrid and El Valle under coaches Serafín Calvo, Rafael Molina and Sonia Caballero.
One of Spain's top age-group swimmers, Leblic represented her country on the Spanish Junior National Team from 2021-23, the Spanish Junior Open Water National Team from 2021-22 and the Spanish Open Water National Team in 2022.
Her accomplishments include a fourth-place finish in the 800-meter freestyle relay at the European Junior Championships and qualification for the European Junior Championships. She was a two-time Spanish junior national champion in the 400 individual medley and 800 freestyle relay, earned eight Spanish junior national medals across individual and relay events, and won junior national titles in the 5-kilometer open water race and 7.5-kilometer open water competition. She also set a national age-group record in the 5-kilometer long-course event.
Leblic compiled an impressive list of regional accomplishments, winning 12 state championships across freestyle, backstroke and individual medley events. She also captured a state title in the 3-kilometer open water race and established a state record in the event.
Most recently, she won national under-20 titles in the 100 freestyle and 200 freestyle, added a bronze medal in the 400 freestyle, captured a national championship in the 200 freestyle and earned six state titles in the 100 freestyle, 200 freestyle, 400 freestyle and 200 individual medley.
Academic Honors

•CSC Academic All-District Team (2025-26)

Leblic is majoring in nutrition with a concentration in dietetics.
A unique connection to the Olympic Games inspired her name. Her parents have attended Olympic Games since Sydney 2000, and she was named Sydney because of their experience there. She has also attended the Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro in 2016 and Paris in 2024.
Outside the pool, she enjoys reading. Her favorite book is A Good Girl's Guide to Murder, and her favorite television show is The Rookie. She lists Canadian swimming star Summer McIntosh as her favorite athlete.

At UNH
Mahon has distinguished herself both in the pool and in the classroom. She earned College Sports Communicators (CSC) Academic All-District honors in 2025 and was a two-time America East All-Academic Team selection (2024-25, 2025-26).

Born in Connecticut and raised in Orange, Connecticut. Daughter of Sean and Anna Mahon. Has a younger brother, Lance, who plays tight end at Stony Brook University.
Mahon is majoring in psychology with minors in leadership and social work. She aspires to become a therapist.

Iris Lizarduy Castillo.b:
Before UNH
A native of Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain, Lizarduy Castillo joins the Wildcats after a decorated club swimming career with Menditxo under coaches Joan Lorente and Aitzol Antolin. She earned Distinction with Honors at Ekialdea BHI, an academic recognition awarded to just seven of 170 students in her graduating class.
One of Spain's top age-group swimmers, she posted multiple podium finishes at the Spanish National Championships. During her senior season in 2025-26, she placed second in her age group in both the 200-meter individual medley and 200-meter butterfly and added a third-place finish in the 100-meter butterfly. As a junior, she won the national title in her age group in the 200-meter individual medley and finished third in the 200-meter butterfly. She also earned national podium finishes in previous years, including second in the 100-meter butterfly and third in the 200-meter butterfly.

Born in Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain, on Dec. 8, 2008. Daughter of Alberto Lizarduy Martínez and María Castillo Gomez de Segura. Has one older brother, Sergio, who is also a swimmer and is studying to become a teacher.

Speaks Spanish and Basque fluently, is proficient in English, and also has knowledge of German. She enjoys learning new languages and hopes to add French and Italian in the future.
Outside of swimming, enjoys reading, surfing, hiking, roller skating, and spending time with friends and family. Her favorite athlete is Spanish swimmer Jessica Vall, while she admires renowned primatologist and conservationist Jane Goodall and Spanish astronaut Sara García.

Kelsey Mayers.b:
At UNH
Mayers earned America East Rookie of the Week honors during her first season with the Wildcats.
Before UNH
Mayers competed at Charlotte Christian School, where she established herself as one of the program's top swimmers. A four-time all-conference selection, she set school records in the 100 butterfly and 100 backstroke during her high school career.
As a senior, Mayers set school records in both the 100 butterfly and 100 backstroke while earning all-conference honors. She also earned all-conference recognition and set the school record in the 100 butterfly during her freshman, sophomore and junior seasons.
Competing for SwimMAC Carolina under coach Kevin Thornton, Mayers developed into a standout student-athlete both in the pool and in the classroom.
Academically, she graduated as the salutatorian of her class, ranking second among 97 students. Her honors included recognition as a Jefferson Scholars semifinalist, the Harvard Book Award and Dean's List with Highest Honors.
Personal
Born in Charlotte, North Carolina. Daughter of David and Kirsten Mayers. Has two older brothers, Reid and Matt.

Swimming is a family tradition. Her grandmother represented Canada at the Olympic Games, providing inspiration for Mayers throughout her athletic career.
Outside the pool, she enjoys scuba diving. Her favorite book is Remarkably Bright Creatures, her favorite movie is Knives Out, and her favorite television show is Psych. She lists Olympic gold medalist Torri Huske as her favorite athlete.
Why UNH?
"My teammates and the friendships I have made."
Fun Fact
Mayers' grandmother competed in the Olympic Games for Canada.

Lily Peterson.b:
Before UNH
Peterson transferred to UNH in 2026-27 after competing for Stonehill College.
At Stonehill
Peterson enjoyed a successful two-year career at Stonehill, where she was a four-time Dean's List selection and earned College Sports Communicators Academic All-District honors.
As a sophomore in 2025-26, she established school records in the 100-yard breaststroke, 200 medley relay and 400 medley relay. At the NEC Championships, she helped Stonehill set school records in both relay events while also setting a program record in the 100 breaststroke (1:04.84) and the 200 breaststroke (2:23.42).
Throughout the season, Peterson earned multiple event victories, including wins in the 100 breaststroke and 200 breaststroke, and was named an NEC Prime Performer. She also contributed to several relay victories and posted a personal-best time of 1:05.95 in the 100 breaststroke.
During her freshman season, Peterson won both the 100 breaststroke and 200 breaststroke against Babson and recorded personal-best performances at a midseason meet hosted by Rhode Island.
A graduate of Concord High School, she excelled both academically and athletically while competing in swimming and track and field.
At Concord High School, Peterson graduated 11th in a class of 375 students and earned summa cum laude honors. She was recognized as an NH Scholar, a Jefferson Scholars semifinalist, a Harvard Book Award recipient and a three-time Principal's Award winner. She also earned High Academic Achievement Awards in German I, German II, History & Geography, AP Biology and AP Environmental Science.
In the pool, Peterson competed for club coach Brian Crawford and qualified for Speedo Sectionals during her senior year. She also competed at the ISCA Swim Meet in Florida and earned high academic honors throughout her high school career.
Personal
Born in Fairbanks, Alaska, and raised in Bow, New Hampshire. Daughter of Chris and Emily Peterson. Has three younger siblings: Corbin, Ivy and Max.
Peterson is majoring in finance and hopes to one day join the finance rotational program at Fidelity Investments. Her athletic goals include qualifying for the National Invitational Championships and ultimately competing at the NCAA Championships.
Outside the pool, Peterson enjoys learning about sports nutrition, weight training, baking, traveling and spending time with friends.
She also serves as a brand ambassador for Bobo's Oat Bars, combining her interests in nutrition and marketing. As part of the program, she received product donations that she shared with younger swimmers in her club community.
Why UNH?
"What I like most about UNH is the balance between strong academics and opportunities to get involved through swimming, leadership programs, networking events and campus organizations while still being close to both the city and the outdoors."

Peterson enjoys cooking and is particularly known for making a variety of pasta dishes.

"What I like most about UNH is the many opportunities it provides both inside and outside the classroom. My majors in marine biology and sustainability have given me hands-on learning and real-world experience, while the university's sustainability initiatives have allowed me to get involved in meaningful work. I also love the sense of community within UNH Athletics and the support I receive from teammates, coaches, professors and the broader UNH community."
Fun Fact
Because her father served in the Navy, Serfass lived in five countries growing up: the United States, Italy, Spain, England and Germany. She learned Italian, Spanish and German while living overseas, joined her first swim team in Spain and even competed in the pool used for the 2012 London Olympics.
f: Marine, Estuarine and Freshwater Biology, Sustainability

Anna Mikish.b:
At UNH
Mikish earned High Honors and Honors recognition during her freshman year at UNH.
Before UNH
Mikish graduated first in her class from the Kharkiv Professional College of Sports in Ukraine, earning magna cum laude honors.
An accomplished swimmer on both the national and international levels, Mikish earned a bronze medal in the 50 butterfly at the 2022 Ukrainian National Championships. She also posted strong performances at major U.S. competitions, including a top-14 finish in the 200 breaststroke at the 2024 Speedo Summer Championships in Irvine, California, and a top-19 finish in the event at the 2024 Winter Junior Championships. She added another top-19 finish in the 200 breaststroke at the 2025 Speedo Summer Championships.
Competing for Phoenix Swim Club under head coach Darian Townsend and assistant coach Michael Maczuga, Mikish was an Arizona State Championship finalist and medalist, a Speedo Sectionals finalist and medalist, and a finalist at both the Winter Junior Championships and Summer Junior Nationals.
Outside the pool, she earned national recognition for her work in animation and digital art, receiving Ukraine's "Hero of the Nation" award in 2024 for her contributions to youth animation.
Personal
Born in Cherkasy, Ukraine, and raised in Kharkiv, Ukraine. Daughter of Serhii and Nadiya Mikish.
She is pursuing a degree in computer science with a cybersecurity option while also minoring in design studies and business administration.
A talented artist and musician, Mikish creates her own animated cartoons, handling the drawing, animation, voice acting and music composition herself. She also graduated from music school with honors as a pianist and earned multiple national and international awards.
Athletic achievement runs throughout her family. Her father, Serhii, ranked among the world's top 10 performers in the 400-meter hurdles, competed for the Ukrainian National Team in the decathlon and earned multiple national medals. Her sister, Angelina, swam collegiately at Grand Canyon University and represented Ukraine internationally, while her brother, Artem, earned success in naval pentathlon competition, including a World Cup silver medal and European championship title.
Outside of athletics, Mikish enjoys animation, art, voice acting and music composition.
Why UNH?
"I absolutely love the location and how it feels like home."
Fun Fact
A lifelong Olympic fan, Mikish says that during the 2008 Beijing Olympics she would "swim" across the floor of her home in full swim gear, practicing flip turns off the walls while pretending to compete.

Claire Thorne.b:
Before UNH
Thorne joins the Wildcats following a successful club and high school career in Ontario, Canada. She attended St. Anne's School in Aurora, Ontario, where she helped lead the Cygnets to a CISAA Open Team Championship.
Competing for the Newmarket Stingrays under coach Edit Varga, Thorne established herself as one of Ontario's top age-group swimmers. During her senior season, she competed at the World Aquatics World Cup and earned a bronze medal in the 100-meter butterfly at the Ontario Age Group Championships.
As a junior, Thorne qualified for the Canadian Junior Trials in the 50-meter breaststroke, reached the finals at the Ontario Swimming Championships and the Speedo Canadian Short Course Championships, and earned a medal at the OFSAA Championships.
Earlier in her career, she earned bronze medals in the 200-meter butterfly at both the Winter Ontario Championships and Speedo Eastern Championships. She also qualified for the Canadian Olympic Junior Trials in the 200-meter butterfly and earned additional OFSAA honors. As a freshman, she captured multiple medals at the Ontario Youth Junior Championships, including silver medals in the 100-meter butterfly, 200-meter butterfly and 200-meter freestyle, while also earning bronze in the 400-meter freestyle and qualifying for the Speedo Canadian Championships.
Thorne also held the Newmarket Stingrays' 12-and-under club record in the 50-meter butterfly.
Academic Honors
Thorne excelled in the classroom, ranking among the top students in her class and earning numerous academic distinctions. Her honors include the Helen Ventin Chemistry Award, UNH Trustee Scholarship, UNH International Student Scholarship, and recognition as a finalist for the Science Ambassador Scholarship.
She was consistently recognized as one of her school's top academic students and qualified for provincial-level robotics competitions in both RoboCup and VEX Robotics. She also placed in the top 25 percent on several University of Waterloo mathematics contests, including the Hypatia, Euclid and Fermat competitions.
Personal
Born in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada. Daughter of Matthew and Tracey Thorne. Has an older brother, Hayden, who studies law in the United Kingdom.
Thorne is pursuing a degree in chemical engineering with a bioengineering concentration and hopes to use her education to make a positive impact on others. She also hopes to continue swimming throughout her life and one day complete a swim across Lake Ontario.
Athletics run in the family. Her brother plays golf at Queen's University Belfast in Northern Ireland. Her father played hockey at Queen's University in Ontario, while her mother competed in synchronized swimming.
Outside the pool, Thorne enjoys crocheting, painting and reading. She often creates clothing, stuffed animals and handmade gifts through crochet projects.
Why UNH?
"I love the location and the people. The mountains, trees and water are incredibly calming, and everyone I met during my visit was welcoming and kind."
Fun Fact
Thorne is an accomplished bagpipe player and enjoys crocheting in her spare time. One of her favorite projects is creating handmade gifts for friends and family.

Genevieve Stephens.b:
Before UNH
Stephens joins the Wildcats following a successful diving and gymnastics career at Clovis West High School in Fresno, California.
A four-time all-conference diver, Stephens helped lead Clovis West to multiple conference and championship titles. As a senior, she earned all-conference honors, was named a Scholar-Athlete and helped the Golden Eagles capture both the TRAC and Valley championships. She also received the Gymnastics Pursuing Victory With Honor Award and earned recognition as a Student of Academic Distinction, a CSF Lifetime Member and a recipient of the Principal's Medallion.
During her junior season, Stephens earned all-conference honors in diving, helped both the swim and dive and gymnastics teams win TRAC championships, and captured a national title in the Break the Barriers 3D One Arrow competition in both the individual and team divisions. As a sophomore, she broke the school's freshman 11-dive record with a score of 388.90, earned the Diving Coaches Award and helped Clovis West win TRAC and Valley championships. She also was named Diving Most Improved Athlete as a freshman.
In addition to her diving accomplishments, Stephens is a national champion archer in Olympic recurve competition and has competed in the sport for four years.
Academically, she graduated near the top of her class, ranking 16th among 517 students. Her honors include AP Scholar recognition, Principal's Honor Roll, Student of Academic Distinction, CSF Lifetime Membership and Scholar-Athlete honors.
Personal
Born in Fresno, California. Daughter of Jeremiah and Christina Stephens. Has an older brother, Lucas.
Stephens plans to study wildlife and conservation biology and hopes to pursue a career as a wildlife biologist while volunteering in wildlife rehabilitation efforts.
Outside of athletics, she enjoys hiking, art, reading, animals and crafts. She particularly enjoys making bracelets and other handmade gifts.
A dedicated volunteer, Stephens has spent the past four years working in her church café, where she learned to prepare a wide variety of coffee and specialty drinks.
Why UNH?
"I love the atmosphere of UNH. As soon as I stepped onto campus, I felt safe, comfortable and at home. The area is beautiful and offers so many opportunities to become a better version of myself."
Fun Fact
No matter where her family travels around the world, they seem to find a friendly cat to pet. Stephens says it has become an unofficial family tradition.

Marisa White.b:
Before UNH
White competed at Apex High School, where she swam for the Cougars and developed into one of the area's top distance freestyle swimmers.
A club swimmer for New Wave Swim Team under coach John Roy, White earned the Rachel Lyon Award and was named Apex High School Varsity Women's Swim MVP. Earlier in her career, she captured the NC Open Water 10K Poseidon title and earned MVP honors with WAVE Swimming.
White also won the South Wake Athletic Conference championship in the 500 freestyle in 2021.
Academic Honors
White earned Honor Roll recognition throughout high school from 2021-24 and was named a North Carolina Scholar.
Personal
Born in North Carolina and raised in Apex, North Carolina. Daughter of Jon and Janis White. Has a brother, Felix, who studies oysters.
White is majoring in environmental science and has a strong interest in the natural world and conservation.
Athletics run in her family. Her grandmother competed on her college tennis team.
Outside the pool, White enjoys art, biking, hiking, reading and exploring the outdoors. Her favorite book is Flowers for Algernon, and her favorite movie is Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle.
She lists teammate Kellie Kasabian as her favorite athlete and says her parents are the people she admires most.
Why UNH?
"The nature."
Fun Fact
White can play the French horn and enjoys combining her artistic and outdoor interests through drawing, hiking and new adventures.

Josh Willman.b:
Josh Willman is currently in his 34th season at the helm of the University of New Hampshire swimming & diving program in 2026-27.
14 X CONFERENCE CHAMPIONS (12 AE AND 2 ECAC)
Willman has led the program to great success during his tenure at UNH. The Wildcats have won the America East Championship in 1998, 1999, 2005, 2006, 2013, 2014, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2025. The 12 championships are the most by a program in conference history. The Wildcats have also earned two ECAC Team Championships (2003 and 2011).
22 X COACH OF THE YEAR (17 AE AND 4 ECAC)
Willman is the America East Conference’s most highly decorated coach. He has been selected America East Coach of the Year a league-record 17 times (1993, 1995, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2002, 2005, 2006, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2025) and ECAC Coach of the Year four times (2003, 2011, 2013 and 2014).
59 MAJOR CONFERENCE AWARDS
New Hampshire swimmers are the most highly honored student-athletes in the America East, winning 57 major conference awards including 27 Swimmers of the Year (19 America East, seven ECAC, one NAC), 12 America East Scholar-Athletes of the Year, 10 Rookies of the Year and 10 Dave Alexander Coaches Awards. During Willman's tenure there have been more than 420 America East champions and 113 ECAC champions. The Wildcats have won 164 individual America East championships and 64 relay titles. UNH has also been a power at the ECAC Championships winning 54 individual titles and 18 relays for 72 total championships. Also three times Willman has coached a swimmer to a gold medal at the CSCAA National Invitational Championships. Wildcat swimmers have broken over 260 school records, 111 America East records and 29 ECAC records.
12 X NCAA QUALIFIERS
Twelve times Willman has coached an athlete that qualified for the Division I NCAA Swimming & Diving Championships. Willman produced UNH’s first-ever NCAA Division I qualifier in 1995 when Denise Leckenby reached the NCAA Championships. She also qualified in 1996 and 1998. She earned All-America honors in 1996, placing eighth in the 200-freestyle and 11th in the 100-freestyle. UNH went on to finish 27th in the nation at the 1996 NCAA Swimming & Diving Championships. Leckenby also was named an All-American in 1998. Shannon Daly (2006), Kary Goodman (2006), Jenni Roberts (2013), Katie Mann (2013, 2014 and 2015) and Anna Metzler (2020, 2021 and 2022) also qualified for the NCAA Championships.
NATIONAL HEIGHTS
Another major milestone that Willman led UNH to was on Feb. 21, 2013 as the national polls were released by CollegeSwimming.com, the Wildcats earned the 19th spot in the rankings. It was the first time UNH was ranked in the top 20 in the Division I Poll. Then on Feb. 18, 2014, the Wildcats were ranked 14th overall in the CollegeSwimming.com Division I national poll, their highest ranking in program history. Among the top-five schools were the University of Georgia (1), Stanford University (2), University of Southern California (3), University of California (4) and University of Florida (5).
OLYMPIC TRIALS
Willman led the program to another major first when he coached New Hampshire native and breaststroke standout Kristen Zeimetz who was a finalist at the 2000 U.S. Open and participated in the 2000 U.S. Olympic team trials. UNH has then gone onto consistently have swimmers compete at the elite level representing not only the United States but more recently in the international arena with Wildcat swimmers competing at Senior Nationals and the Olympic Trials for their home countries including Canada, South Africa and Denmark.
ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE
New Hampshire is consistently an Academic All-America team and swimmers have earned NCAA Academic All-American honors, post-graduate scholarship awards and ranked as high as sixth nationally for grade point average.
Willman began his coaching career just after graduating from Miami when he coached at the YMCA and U.S.A. Swimming level. He entered the collegiate coaching arena as the assistant coach for New Hampshire in 1991, taking over the program the following season when he earned his first coaching honor as the Men’s Coach of the Year in 1992-1993. Willman is a certified ASCA Level IV coach and has been a recipient of the ASCA Coaching Excellence Award.

Derek Peabody.b:
Derek Peabody joined the UNH Swimming and Diving program as assistant diving coach in the summer of 2026 under the direction of head diving coach Dr. Rick Schavone.
Derek brings more than a decade of coaching experience spanning the club, high school, and collegiate ranks. He is the owner and head coach of Dive 603d LLC, a USA Diving- and AAU-sanctioned club he founded in 2023. Under his leadership, the program has quickly emerged as a competitive presence in New England, producing seven AAU national qualifiers and preparing divers for success at the regional and national levels, with several advancing to collegiate competition.
Derek has coached extensively throughout New Hampshire and Massachusetts, guiding numerous high school athletes to state championships and postseason success. His coaching background also includes work within the New England Preparatory School Athletic Council (NEPSAC) and a previous collegiate coaching role at Keene State College, where he helped develop divers at the NCAA Division-III level.
As a student-athlete at Keene State, Derek earned Top-5 finishes at both the New England Intercollegiate Swimming and Diving Association (NEISDA) Championships and the ECAC Open. He was a four-time All-New England honoree, a two-year team captain, and recorded multiple Top-5 placements at the MIAA Division I Championships during his high school career at Haverhill (Mass.) High School.
Known for his technical expertise, athlete-centered coaching style, and proven ability to develop divers from foundational skills to collegiate-ready competitors, Derek brings strong energy and a deep developmental background to the Wildcats’ diving program.
Derek lives in Nashua with his wife and two young daughters.

Nicole Benson.b:
Nicole Benson returned for her third tenure as an assistant coach under Josh Willman in 2025-26. Previously, she was a volunteer assistant coach from 2004-11 before returning as a volunteer assistant for the 2018 season. She was part of three UNH America East Championships: 2013, 2014 and 2018.
Benson returned to UNH from Phillips Exeter Academy, where she served as an assistant varsity swim coach at one of the most exclusive private schools in the world from 2018-25. Her leadership played a major factor in the success of a team that produced incredibly talented high school and age-group swimmers at the regional, national and, as of this past spring, international level.
Benson was a standout swimmer at the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay where she swam sprint freestyle and backstroke events for three seasons. She still holds multiple top-10 times at UWGB and was inducted into the school’s Hall of Fame in 2002. She went on to complete her eligibility at the University of Kansas, where she earned her Master’s degree in Sociology.
Benson started her coaching career as a graduate assistant for Kansas and assistant masters swimming coach in Lawrence, Kansas, in 1997 and 1998. She later became the head swimming coach for the YMCA Green Dolphins Swimming club in Wausau, Wisconsin. She also worked as an assistant swimming coach for the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point, where she assisted in recruiting and worked specifically with the sprint group.
After moving to the Seacoast area in the early 2000s, Benson became a huge force within the local swimming community. She initially coached with the Portsmouth High School swim team before launching the Newmarket High School swim program.
During her previous UNH experiences, Benson was part of the coaching staff for Wildcat teams that featured numerous America East record holders and NCAA qualifiers including Amy Perrault and Liza Baykova as well as UNH Hall of Famer Shannon Daly and Melissa Lague. She also coached club swimming, first with the Exeter Swim team, then Commonwealth Current North, formerly SOLO Aquatics (SOLO), which offers year-round competitive swim and dive programs to athletes ages 6 to 21.
Benson and her husband Tom have five children: Andrew, Amy, Alison, Anika and Ada. Amy is a rising college junior and swims for Trinity University in San Antonio, Texas, where she is a Division III All-American. Andrew, whose name can be found on the Swasey Pool record board, just completed his fifth year at the University of Wisconsin, where he was a three-year NCAA qualifier and two-time Olympic Trials qualifier. Alison is entering her first year at the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse and will swim for the Eagles.

Dr. Rick Schavone.b:
The Wildcats welcome UNH Hall of Famer Dr. Rick Schavone back to New England as the head diving coach. A 1971 graduate of New Hampshire, Schavone spent over 35 years coaching at Stanford University where he molded Stanford into one of the top all-around diving programs in the nation.
A four-time NCAA Diving Coach of the Year, Schavone is also an eight-time recipient of the Pac-12 Diving Coach of the Year award. Schavone served on Team USA's Olympic coaching staff at the 2012 Olympics after two of his divers earned their first Olympic nods. Kristian Ipsen won the bronze medal in the 3-meter synchro at the 2012 Olympic Games in London and Cassidy Krug placed seventh off the 3-meter springboard. He has coach divers to NCAA national championship titles 12 times and runners-up 6 times.
In addition to his work at Stanford, Schavone has served as the head coach for numerous United States diving teams and has traveled all over the world as head coach or assisting at FINA World Championships, World Cups, World University Games, Goodwill Games, European Championships and nearly every international meet imaginable.
Schavone has also held many positions with USA Diving and received numerous awards, perhaps most notable the prestigious Whosam Award in 2003, given annually to a coach that adheres to the highest standards of physical and mental well-being.
Upon retirement from Stanford, Schavone traveled down under to work with the Australian National Program from 2018-2022 where he assisted with the tutelage of their elite divers among them World Champion Matthew Carter and Olympian Nikita Hains.
Most recently, Schavone was a volunteer coach at the University of Texas working alongside Matt Scoggin and the great Longhorn divers.
We are thrilled and humbled to have Dr. Rick Schavone on deck working with our divers, it is an incredible opportunity for both the student-athletes and the entire coaching staff to learn from this legendary coach.
